title: Validation Stack — rulings 1-9
summary: No silent refusal, severity/text held low and display-blind, fold bubbling as an IDE red-folder, one 1-D address unifying marks and the pill, and drag-time validity preview on by default — the same fixtures driven through DOM Canvas, React Flow and tldraw.
intro: What the oracles observed by actually running maxGraph and JointJS is the strongest evidence this spec rests on, and it changed real decisions: maxGraph's Multiplicity.check was the planned type-vocabulary donor and was REJECTED after running it — checkTerminal(graph, source_or_target, edge) receives the connecting EDGE in the parameter named terminal (Multiplicity.ts:147-150 vs the call site at :204-208, v0.24.0), so it silently no-ops for every ordinary edge, reproduced against maxGraph's own shipped Validation-story fixtures. Blockly's list-intersection shape (ConnectionChecker.doTypeChecks, fetched from GitHub) replaced it. JointJS's own dangling-edge demo and its markAvailable lifecycle (RAN live) are the behaviour-derived donors for the 1-D address and the once-per-gesture availability contract; JointJS's ToolsView has ZERO collision handling (two tools landed on the identical pixel, RAN) — the citation for why separateAlongPath is ours, ad hoc.

This lane merged two already-landed lanes (scene: edgeValidation/lint/availability/bubble; component: trace path-addressing, TraceMark, Port availability) into one worktree, ran pnpm typecheck immediately per the dispatch's own warning, and it was clean both times — no import edge the two write sets missed.

One real integration gap DID surface, and it wasn't in either lane's diff: blockPort.tsx's default port renderer never forwarded PortEdgeItem.diagnostics/.availability to the Port/LabeledPort it renders — a file neither lane's write set touched. ValidityPreview.stories.tsx's own failing assertion caught it, not a code review; the fix and its provenance are in docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md's new section.
changes: src/hosts/nodeViews.tsx — new Decorate/SceneNodeDecoration seam: one node in, optional {diagnostics, availability, portDiagnostics} out. undefined decorate = byte-identical to every pre-existing story.
src/hosts/domCanvas.tsx, reactFlowHost.tsx, tldrawHost.tsx — each threads the new decorate prop straight to SceneNodeView, adds-only.

src/components/blockPort.tsx — renderItem and renderCollapsed now forward item.diagnostics/item.availability (new collapsedDiagnostics/collapsedAvailability helpers, modelled on the file's own pre-existing collapsedState "any wired wins" shape) — the integration fix above.

src/stories/ValidityPreview.stories.tsx — new: ruling 5, a real pointer gesture through DomCanvas. Legal targets marked at drag-start (once, never per-pointermove), a preview Trace coloured by a LOOKUP against the held map, invalid release commits nothing, and a pre-existing many-to-one mark on sink/in survives every gesture untouched (prevention is additive, never a replacement).

src/stories/FoldBubbling.stories.tsx — new: ruling 3, the IDE red-folder case. Two independent cycle findings on two hidden members bubble together onto the one ancestor that hides them; a hypothetical fifth view ("peek", not even in the app's own BlockView union) bubbles correctly as one local table row, with zero import from or string added to bubble.ts.

src/stories/TraceMark.stories.tsx — new: ruling 4, the unified 1-D address. Fractions (including the OURS negative-fraction form, t = 1 + f), a mark pinned {px: -24} from a dangling edge's broken end, and a real pill-collision yield measured on-screen.

src/stories/ValidationHosts.stories.tsx — new: ruling 8/gesture transfer. The SAME connectionAvailability map, painted through the SAME decorate seam, via a real drag on React Flow and a Storybook-control (honestly labelled NOT a gesture) on tldraw.
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — appended this lane's own provenance table, including the blockPort.tsx integration-gap row.
docs/REFERENCE-IMPLEMENTATIONS.md — new: the spec's own embedded reference doc, split out to its own file (the task's ${args.refsDoc} placeholder arrived unsubstituted).
findings: Both merges (scene lane 9e3db3a, component lane c3fbc35) were clean — no conflicts, and pnpm typecheck was green IMMEDIATELY after, before a single story was written, per the dispatch's own warning about lanes passing separately and failing together.

The blockPort.tsx gap is real and load-bearing, not a story-only fixture issue: PortEdgeItem has carried diagnostics/availability since the component lane's port.tsx/portEdge.tsx/labeledPort.tsx work landed, but the file that actually RENDERS a rail's items (untouched by either lane, not in either lane's declared write set) dropped both fields on the floor. Caught by a real, failing browser test (pnpm test-stories), not inferred from reading the diff.

A drag target that is ALREADY many-to-one at rest correctly reads unavailable for every future candidate too (lint.ts's own many-to-one rule counts distinct sources on the hypothetical scene) — the first ValidityPreview fixture accidentally targeted such a port and the story had to add a second, clean port (sink/in2) to demonstrate the legal-target path; the already-broken port (sink/in) stays the at-rest-grammar demo instead. This is correct behaviour, not a bug — inviting a THIRD wire into an already-illegal port is not "legal" either.

Gesture transfer, measured: the identical connectionAvailability map, painted through the identical decorate seam, produces the identical data-availability attributes on sink/in2 (available) and str/out (unavailable) whether the host is DomCanvas or React Flow — same selectors, same assertions, same result.

tldraw's host (tldrawHost.tsx) has no cable-drawing gesture at all — grepped, no pointerdown-driven edge creation exists anywhere in that file — so simulating one would have fabricated behaviour the host doesn't have. The control-driven story says so on-screen, verbatim, per the dispatch's own required label.

Gate run twice to rule out flake: pnpm exec vitest --project=unit run — 623/623 both times. pnpm test-stories — 243/243 across all 56 story files, both times (one earlier run also showed an unrelated, pre-existing DragPolicy.stories.tsx flake that passed clean on rerun — not touched by this lane).

Per-lane write-set check: git diff --name-only for this commit touches only src/hosts/**, src/stories/** (4 new files), src/components/blockPort.tsx (the one declared deviation, justified above and in ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md), and the two docs files — no magnet*, no batchWire*, no package.json, no pnpm-lock.yaml.
